content.text:
Training features confirm a tight picture:

- Across all 12 examples, every default-accepted fusion has ratio fusedWork/originalWork ≤ ~1.0171 (many are big wins down to 0.5); the single default-rejected decision is example 5: originalWork 257376 → fusedWork 272736, ratio ≈ 1.0596.
- The aggregate features are almost perfectly collinear with the ratio itself: producerElements and consumerCount don't separate good from bad decisions (the bad one has producerElements 1024, the same value as many good ones). attempt-0002 tried to split on producerElements and lost 11% — that path is a dead end. attempt-0003 (threshold 1.0, i.e., reject all growth) also lost ~4%, showing near-neutral fusions are net-positive.
- attempt-0004 (a region guess) tied baseline at 1.0.

So the discriminating dimension is essentially only the ratio boundary near 1.02, which the aggregate threshold already expresses optimally. Honest assessment: **this grammar looks nearly saturated for aggregate work-ratio control.** Trees can only re-express correlations that already exist; region/selective policies add launch/materialization/consumer modeling that the traces don't let me calibrate, so those are structural probes, not claimed speedups.
